queryForm.longRunningHint: Enable for slow queries. They run as a background job the page polls for, so they are not cut off by proxy/gateway timeouts. Normal queries run instantly and should leave this off.
queryForm.allowNoConfirmHint: Only applies to write queries (INSERT/UPDATE/DELETE). When on, users get a "Run directly without preview" checkbox that commits the change in one pass. Turn it off to force every run through the row preview and confirmation step.
queryForm.saveOldValuesHint: Only applies to UPDATE/DELETE queries. When on, every affected row is snapshotted into the execution log so the previous values can be reviewed later. Turn it off for statements that affect large numbers of rows — the snapshot costs an extra SELECT on each run and stores a copy of every affected row.
queryForm.wordTemplateHint: Optional .docx used when this query's results are exported as Word. Put {{results}} where the result table should go; {{queryName}}, {{generatedAt}} and {{rowCount}} are also replaced (including in headers/footers). Each parameter's value is available as {{parameter}} — the same @name you use in the SQL — and {{params}} prints every parameter as "Display Name: value", one per line. To style the result table, put {{results}} inside a table: its first row styles the header, the marker's row styles the data rows, and an optional row below it styles alternating rows. Without a template, the system default Word template is used (managed on the Dynamic Queries page).
queryForm.noTemplate: No template — the default layout is used
queryForm.multiDropdownHint: Selected values are expanded into {{expansion}} at execution time. Use {{inClause}} in your SQL.
queryForm.multiStringHint: User enters comma-separated values (e.g. {{example}}); each is bound as a separate parameter and expanded into {{expansion}}. Use {{inClause}} in your SQL.
queryForm.exportHint: Which formats this query's results may be downloaded as. A person also needs the matching export permission on their role, so this narrows what is possible rather than granting it. Tick nothing to switch downloads off for this query entirely.
queryForm.exportDisabled: Export is off for this query — no download button is shown.

settings.title: System Settings
settings.directoryEnabledHint: Turn this off on an installation with no directory: it hides the AD Users page, which could otherwise only ever report a connection failure. Signing in is not affected — accounts already imported keep authenticating against the directory.
settings.accessTokenMinutesHint: How long a sign-in lasts before the application quietly renews it. Shorter means a revoked account, or someone removed from a group, loses what their token still carries sooner.
settings.refreshTokenDaysHint: How long someone may stay away and still return without signing in again. Must be at least as long as the access token.
settings.maxRows: Row limit for previews and lookups
settings.maxRowsHint: Caps what is read in one go on the paths that hold a whole result in memory: the preview of a write query, the before-change snapshot it records, and the options behind a dropdown parameter. The results grid is not affected — it caches the full result and pages through it — and exports are never capped.

permissions.intro: Every capability the system offers, and which roles hold it. Admin always holds everything and cannot be edited — that is what keeps this page reachable. Changes take effect on the next request; nobody has to sign in again.
